recordStatus: TWO SWEEPS. The top-level body of this file is SWEEP-1, unedited: its FAIL at P2 stands as recorded. Sweep-2 is appended under `sweep2` and does not overwrite, rescore or withdraw any part of it. Read `sweep2.whatSweep1sFailureActuallyWas` for what sweep-1 measured.
headline: FIVE OF SIX POSES PASS. P2 — the only oblique pose, and the one reconstructed from the user's own session — FAILS the member-level half of the verdict rule. The promotion is NOT activated and the default flip is REVERTED.

executedBy.browser: ORCA EMBEDDED BROWSER (orca goto / orca eval / orca screenshot), Orca 1.4.184.
executedBy.whyNotChrome: The Chrome extension browser could not reach this host in any configuration tested: 127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1] and the LAN address all returned ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED from the page context while the same URLs returned 200 from the shell, across two ports, three binding modes, with stale listeners eliminated and no system proxy configured. It reached https://example.com in the same second. The instrument is the DOM state, so any browser on this host is a valid vehicle; which one ran it is recorded here for honesty.
executedBy.server: vite dev, 127.0.0.1:4173, serving the staged tier (1,681 files).

attemptDisclosure.statement: THE REGISTERED POLICY WAS ONE ATTEMPT PER POSE. THREE PASSES WERE RUN, AND EVERY ONE IS DISCLOSED HERE. Two instrument defects were found by the sweep itself and neither reading was a verdict on the tier.
attemptDisclosure.attempt1: The member-level metric compared the FULL member list of every drawn tile against the applied-alpha set and read 41,405 uncovered at P1. Meaningless: alpha can only be written for buildings the dense index HOLDS, and most members of the island's tiles have no massing primitive loaded. A building that is not drawing cannot show tan. The metric was rescoped to loaded massing.
attemptDisclosure.attempt2: The settle detector accepted six stable 500 ms samples. The attribute set plateaus mid-flight during a dense-layer rebuild, so it fired early and reported states that were still moving.
attemptDisclosure.attempt3: AUTHORITATIVE. Corrected metric, and a settle rule requiring four consecutive identical full-attribute reads at 6 s spacing with a 48 s minimum dwell. These are the readings below.
attemptDisclosure.whyThisIsNotShoppingForAPass: The corrections made the instrument measure the declared quantity; they did not move a bar. P2 still FAILS under the corrected instrument, and it failed under every one of the three.

verdictRule: Per pose: over-budget = absent = checksum-mismatch = build-failure = 0, AND every V3T-eligible member either near/mid-drawn, suppressed under a drawn tile, or in the committed exemption set.
notDeclaredIsAnExemption: Every ON pose reports notDeclared = 1. It is the Block 835 alias cell, whose id encodes no tile rectangle and which is named in the committed exemption set for exactly this reason.

whatSweep1sFailureActuallyWas.verdictOnSweep1: SWEEP-1'S P2 FAIL IS NOT WITHDRAWN. It is preserved above, unedited. What changed is the explanation of it.
whatSweep1sFailureActuallyWas.mechanism: `publishFarTierState()` was called at the moment the drawn-cell set advanced — before `farTierCovered` was computed and before `applyFarTierAlpha` wrote anything. The published reading therefore paired a NEW drawn set with the PREVIOUS pass's applied-alpha set, and since the pass never published again, that stale reading stood as the last word.
evidence: Instrumented at the seam on the failing pose: the selection pass itself reported passUncovered = 0 at the same instant the published attribute read thousands.
desiredCovered == appliedCovered throughout, so not one alpha write was ever skipped — the 'lost write' hypothesis is excluded by measurement, not by argument.
Every uncovered id classified as `notDesired` (the covered set never contained it), with `uncoveredDesired` and `uncoveredHidden` both 0.
The published drawn count (839) exceeded the drawn set the last pass had actually selected over (776) — the two halves of the reading were one pass apart.
Reproduced deterministically on a cold cache: 6,145 uncovered, stable for 80 s, never healing — a STUCK stale reading, not an intermittent race.
whatSweep1sFailureActuallyWas.consequence: The scene was correct at P2 the entire time. The number was not. This was an INSTRUMENT defect, which is the third one this metric has had, and that history is why sweep-2 publishes `passUncovered` as a permanent selection-time control alongside the published figure.
whatSweep1sFailureActuallyWas.whatWasNotTheCause: NOT the dense-rebuild / covered-set race the failure resembled and that sweep-1 pointed at. That hypothesis was tested and excluded.

otherObservation.uiErrors: The six repeated `Unexpected token '<', "<!doctype "... is not valid JSON` notices sweep-1 recorded as UNDIAGNOSED are now DIAGNOSED.
otherObservation.cause: Six exterior SERVING releases are declared by src/release/exterior-serving-waves.ts — manhattan-exterior-cells-20260811-v3-s1, -midtown-core-...-v3-s1, -lower-manhattan-...-s1, -southern-remainder-...-s1, -central-upper-manhattan-...-s1, -northern-manhattan-...-s1. None of the six exists on disk in this worktree or in the main checkout: they are generated, gitignored local data. The dev/preview SPA fallback answers /data/<id>/release.json with index.html, and JSON.parse reports the `<!doctype` token. Six declared packages, six errors, one per package.
otherObservation.verifiedHow: curl of all six manifest paths against the same server that served the sweep returned '<!doctype h' for every one; `ls public/data/*-s1` matches nothing.
otherObservation.attribution: NOT the far tier, and NOT introduced by T005. A pre-existing missing-local-data condition.
otherObservation.notFixedHere: Producing those packages means running an acquisition/normalization/build/publish workflow, which AGENTS.md places outside ordinary setup and behind an explicitly approved operator workflow. It was NOT run.
otherObservation.consequenceForThisSweep: MATERIAL AND DISCLOSED: the exterior LOD-0 wave tier was ABSENT from the vehicle for BOTH sweeps. The sweep therefore measures the dense massing tier and the far tier and their interaction; it does NOT measure the three-tier composition with exterior waves present. That is a real gap in what this sweep can support, and it applies equally to sweep-1's five passes.

consequence.rollback: One token back to false. What that restores is the pre-HLOD COMPOSITION — massing and mid ring, no far-tier fetches — and NOT the raised residency ceilings or the swapped inventory pin, both of which stay in the build. That is a third configuration nobody has measured.
